issues: Spelling guidance says the silent 'gh' is 'in the middle', but it comes near the end, just before the final 't', so this could confuse young spellers.
The collocation 'straight home' uses a different sense ('without stopping or delay'), which the simple meaning does not cover.
suggested_fixes: Rephrase as: "Straight has a silent 'gh' before the last 't': s-t-r-a-i-g-h-t."
Either replace 'straight home' with 'straight on', or add a short note: "'Go straight home' means go home without stopping anywhere."
